feature: Undo after clicking something in the right hand panel
summary: A report said Command Z did nothing after clicking a control in the right hand panel. It turns out no scripted walk can press Command Z at all, with or without a panel click, so the walks were never evidence about the app. What a walk can check now passes: a panel change goes on the undo stack and Undo takes it back. The one thing the loop cannot check is the keystroke itself in a real, frontmost app, which is this audit's whole ask.
setup: Photonz Dev, any document. Nothing to turn on.

try.do: Draw a rectangle with the Rectangle tool.
Switch to the Select tool so the rectangle is selected.
Click the Fill switch in the right hand panel, turning Fill off.
Press Command Z once, without clicking the canvas first.
Press Command Z again and watch the rectangle itself go.

evaluate: Did the first Command Z put the Fill switch back on?
Did it take exactly one press, or did you have to click the canvas first to give the keyboard back?
Does Command Z also take back a change made from a panel menu, like Blending set to Multiply?
When it does undo, does anything on screen tell you what was undone, or do you have to spot it?
rough: No pictures with this one: the Mac's screen was locked for the whole task, so macOS refuses every window capture, and the offscreen renders would have shown nothing about a keystroke anyway.

The loop cannot answer question one by itself, today or ever: macOS refuses a script-launched app the focus that Command Z needs, proven four ways on 2026-09-03. So if undo really does fail for you here, a person has to say so, and this audit is the place.

The walks that started this were fine as walks and wrong as evidence. Their log line now names Edit > Undo and says the item is dimmed and empty, so the next runner reads the reason instead of filing the app.
